nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-01.title: Parity
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-01.body:
If all four primes were odd, their sum would be even. The sum divides the product, so the product would be even too; but a product of four odd numbers is odd. Hence one of the primes is even, i.e. equal to $2$, and $2$ is then the smallest of the four. Such a set exists: $2+3+11+17=33$ divides $2\cdot3\cdot11\cdot17=1122=33\cdot34$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-02.title: Track the angle
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-02.body:
At 6:00 the hands are $180^\circ$ apart. After $r$ minutes the minute hand has turned $6r$ degrees and the hour hand $\frac r2$ degrees, so (before the minute hand passes the hour hand) the angle between them is $180-6r+\frac r2=180-\frac{11r}{2}$ degrees. Setting this equal to $90$ gives $\frac{11r}{2}=90$, $r=\frac{180}{11}=16\frac4{11}$ minutes.

**Answer: $6{:}16\frac{4}{11}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-02.title: Relative speed
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-02.body:
The minute hand gains $5.5^\circ$ per minute on the hour hand. It must close the gap from $180^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, i.e. gain $90^\circ$, which takes $\frac{90}{5.5}=\frac{180}{11}=16\frac{4}{11}$ minutes.

**Answer: $6{:}16\frac{4}{11}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-03.title: Intersecting chords
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-03.body:
Let $X$ be the midpoint of $AB$; the diameter through $M$ passes through $X$ and is perpendicular to $AB$. Triangle $AXM$ is right with $AX=12$, $AM=13$, so $XM=5$. The diameter through $M$ is cut by $AB$ into pieces $5$ and $2r-5$, and by intersecting chords $5(2r-5)=12\cdot12=144$. So $10r=169$ and $r=\frac{169}{10}$. (The originally printed key had a misprint; the league's correction letter gives $169/10$.)

**Answer: $\frac{169}{10}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-03.title: Right triangle with the center
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-03.body:
Let $O$ be the center. Then $OX=r-5$ and $OA=r$, so $r^2=(r-5)^2+12^2$, giving $10r=169$, $r=16.9$.

**Answer: $\frac{169}{10}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-05.title: Square both sides
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-05.body:
Squaring gives $2x+2\sqrt{x^2-(2x-1)}=2$, i.e. $2x+2\sqrt{(x-1)^2}=2$, so $2x+2|x-1|=2$. For $x\ge1$ this reads $4x-2=2$, so $x=1$. For $x<1$ it reads $2=2$, so every $x$ with $\frac12\le x<1$ (where the radicals are defined) works. The largest solution is $x=1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-05.title: Denest the radicals
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-05.body:
With $t=\sqrt{2x-1}\ge0$, $x=\frac{t^2+1}{2}$, so $x\pm t=\frac{(t\pm1)^2}{2}$. The equation becomes $\frac{|t-1|+(t+1)}{\sqrt2}=\sqrt2$, i.e. $|t-1|+t+1=2$, which holds exactly for $0\le t\le1$. So $2x-1\le1$, $x\le1$, and the largest $x$ is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-06.title: Complex numbers
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-06.body:
$\operatorname{Arctan}\frac13$ is the argument of $3+i$. Then $(3+i)^2=8+6i$ and $(8+6i)^2=28+96i$, whose argument has tangent $\frac{96}{28}=\frac{24}{7}$.

**Answer: $\frac{24}{7}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-07.title: 30-60-90 triangle
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-07.body:
Tangent lengths are equal, so $PO=2PX$. In right triangle $PXO$ (right angle at $X$) the hypotenuse is twice the leg $PX$, so $\cos\angle XPO=\frac12$ and $\angle XPO=60^\circ$. By symmetry $\angle XPY=2\cdot60^\circ=120^\circ$.

**Answer: $120^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-08.title: Substitute $y=x^2$
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-08.body:
If $x$ is a root of $f$, then $y=x^2$ satisfies $y+10=6x$, i.e. $6\sqrt y=y+10$ for the appropriate square root. Squaring: $y^2+20y+100=36y$, so $y^2-16y+100=0$. Thus $(a,b)=(-16,100)$.

**Answer: $(-16,100)$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-08.title: Vieta
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-08.body:
The roots of $f$ are $r,s$ with $r+s=6$, $rs=10$. Then $r^2+s^2=36-20=16$ and $r^2s^2=100$, so $g(x)=x^2-16x+100$. (Indeed $r,s=3\pm i$ and $r^2,s^2=8\pm6i$.)

**Answer: $(-16,100)$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-09.title: Area of a right triangle
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-09.body:
The line meets the axes at $A=(0,5)$ and $B=(10,0)$, so $AB=\sqrt{125}=5\sqrt5$. The radius is the altitude from $O$ to $AB$; computing the area of $OAB$ two ways, $\frac12\cdot5\cdot10=\frac12\cdot5\sqrt5\cdot h$, so $h=\frac{10}{\sqrt5}=2\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt5$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-10.title: Divisibility by 8 and 11
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-10.body:
The number must be divisible by $8$ and by $11$. For $8$: the last three digits $75b$ must be a multiple of $8$; checking, only $752=8\cdot94$ works, so $b=2$. For $11$: the alternating sum $2-5+7-9+a=a-5$ must be a multiple of $11$; since $a$ is a digit, $a=5$. Check: $59752=88\cdot679$.

**Answer: $(5,2)$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-12.title: Identify the segment
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-12.body:
Plane $AMD$ contains line $AD$, hence $N$; it also contains $M$. Likewise plane $BNC$ contains $M$ (on $BC$) and $N$. So the line of intersection is $MN$, and the part inside the tetrahedron is segment $MN$. In triangle $AMN$, $AM=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ (median of the equilateral face $ABC$), $AN=\frac12$, and $MN\perp AD$ because $AM=DM$. So $MN=\sqrt{\frac34-\frac14}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-12.title: Coordinates
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-12.body:
Place the tetrahedron at alternate vertices of a cube of edge $s$; then edges are $s\sqrt2=1$, and the segment joining midpoints of opposite edges $BC$ and $AD$ is parallel to a cube edge with length $s=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-14.title: Find the cycle
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-14.body:
Computing: $a_2=4^3=64$, $a_3=216+64=280$, $a_4=8+512=520$, $a_5=125+8=133$, $a_6=1+27+27=55$, $a_7=125+125=250$, $a_8=8+125=133$. From $a_5$ on the sequence cycles $133,55,250$ with period $3$, so $a_n=133$ whenever $n\equiv2\pmod 3$, $n\ge5$. Since $1985=3\cdot661+2$, $a_{1985}=133$. (The originally printed key said 250; the league's correction letter gives 133.)

**Answer: 133**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-15.title: Factor
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-15.body:
With sides $a,b$: $ab=2a+2b-1$, so $ab-2a-2b+4=3$, i.e. $(a-2)(b-2)=3$. With positive integer sides the factors are $1\cdot3$ (negative factors would make a side $\le 1$ and fail), so the sides are $3$ and $5$ and the area is $15$.

**Answer: 15**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-15.title: Discriminant
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-15.body:
Let $q=a+b$; then $ab=2q-1$, so $a,b$ are roots of $x^2-qx+2q-1=0$, whose discriminant $q^2-8q+4=(q-4)^2-12$ must be a perfect square $N^2$. Then $(q-4-N)(q-4+N)=12$ with factors of equal parity, forcing $q-4=4$, $q=8$, and $a,b=5,3$.

**Answer: 15**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-16.title: Chase angles
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-16.body:
Let $\angle A=a$. Triangle $ADB$ is isosceles, so $\angle ABD=a$ and $\angle BDC=2a$ (exterior angle). Triangle $BDC$ is isosceles with $BD=BC$, so $\angle C=\angle BDC=2a$. Since $AB=AC$, $\angle B=\angle C=2a$. Then $a+2a+2a=180$, so $a=36$.

**Answer: $36^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-17.title: Complete the square
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-17.body:
$n^2+2n+1=(n+1)^2$ ends in $5$, so $n+1$ ends in $5$, say $n+1=10k+5$. Then $(n+1)^2=100k^2+100k+25$ ends in $25$, and $n^2+2n$ ends in $24$. The tens digit is $2$.

**Answer: 2**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-18.title: Remaining lengths
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-18.body:
Take the candle length as $1$. After $t$ hours the remaining lengths are $1-\frac t5$ and $1-\frac t4$. The slower candle is the longer one, so $1-\frac t5=5\left(1-\frac t4\right)$. Then $\frac{5t}{4}-\frac t5=4$, $\frac{21t}{20}=4$, $t=\frac{80}{21}$ hours.

**Answer: $\frac{80}{21}$ hours**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-19.title: Ignore the tail
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-19.body:
For $k\ge5$, $k!$ contains the factors $2$ and $5$ and ends in $0$. So the units digit is that of $1+2+6+24=33$, namely $3$.

**Answer: 3**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-20.title: Similar triangles
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-20.body:
Since $\angle AMN=90^\circ$, $\angle BAM=\angle CMN$, so right triangles $ABM$ and $MCN$ are similar. Then $\frac{AB}{BM}=\frac{MC}{CN}=2$, so $CN=\frac12MC=\frac14BC=\frac14CD$. Hence $CN:ND=1:3$.

**Answer: $1:3$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-22.title: Sequential choices
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-22.body:
The letters must alternate. Whatever the first letter, the second must differ from it: probability $\frac23$ (two of the three remaining tiles). Then the third must differ from the second: probability $\frac12$. The last is forced. Probability $\frac23\cdot\frac12=\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-22.title: Count arrangements
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-22.body:
All $\binom42=6$ arrangements of TTOO are equally likely; only TOTO and OTOT separate both pairs, giving $\frac26=\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-23.title: Double angle
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-23.body:
$\cos^4x+\sin^4x=(\cos^2x+\sin^2x)^2-2\sin^2x\cos^2x=1-\frac12\sin^22x$. Setting this to $\frac34$ gives $\sin^22x=\frac12$; since $0<2x<\pi$, $\sin2x=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$, so $2x=\frac\pi4$ or $\frac{3\pi}{4}$. Thus $x=\frac\pi8$ or $x=\frac{3\pi}{8}$. (The league's correction letter accepts both values.)

**Answer: $\frac{\pi}{8}$ and $\frac{3\pi}{8}$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-25.title: One answer must be a lie
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-25.body:
The two answers name different days (January 4 and January 5), so they cannot both be true; one of them was given on his birthday. If his birthday were January 4, the answer on January 6 (not his birthday) would be truthful and would have been 'the day before yesterday'. So he lied on January 5, which is his birthday; and on January 6 he truthfully said 'yesterday', i.e. January 5.

**Answer: January 5**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-26.title: Sophie Germain factorization
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-26.body:
$n^4+4=(n^2+2)^2-(2n)^2=(n^2+2n+2)(n^2-2n+2)$. Both factors are at least $1$, so for a prime one of them must equal $1$: $(n\pm1)^2+1=1$ forces $n=\pm1$, giving $p=5$. So $5$ is the only such prime, hence the largest.

**Answer: 5**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-27.title: Cyclic quadrilateral
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-27.body:
Triangles $O_1PY$ and $O_2PX$ are isosceles, and their base angles at $P$ are vertical angles ($\angle O_1PY=\angle O_2PX$), so the two triangles are similar and $\angle O_1YO_2=\angle O_1XO_2$. Hence $O_1,Y,X,O_2$ are concyclic, and $\angle XYO_2=\angle XO_1O_2$ (they subtend the same arc $XO_2$). Now $\angle XO_1O_2=\angle PO_1O_2$, which is half of the central angle $\angle PO_1Q=100^\circ$, because $O_1O_2$ bisects $\angle PO_1Q$. So $\angle XYP=50^\circ$.

**Answer: $50^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-28.title: Tangent addition
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-28.body:
Since $18^\circ+42^\circ=60^\circ$, $\sqrt3=\tan60^\circ=\frac{\tan18^\circ+\tan42^\circ}{1-\tan18^\circ\tan42^\circ}$. So $\tan18^\circ+\tan42^\circ=\sqrt3-\sqrt3\tan18^\circ\tan42^\circ$, and the expression equals $\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-29.title: Tangential quadrilateral
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-29.body:
Let $AB=AC=a$, $BC=b$. Quadrilateral $BCNM$ is circumscribed about the circle, so $MN+BC=MB+NC$. With $MN=\frac b2$ (midline) and $MB=NC=\frac a2$: $\frac{3b}{2}=a$, so $AB:BC=3:2$.

**Answer: $3:2$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-29.title: Inradius and heights
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-29.body:
$MN$ is tangent to the incircle and parallel to $BC$, at height $\frac h2$ above $BC$, where $h$ is the altitude from $A$. So the incircle's diameter is $\frac h2$, i.e. $r=\frac h4$. Also $r=\frac{\text{Area}}{s}=\frac{bh/2}{a+b/2}$. Then $\frac{b}{2a+b}=\frac14$, so $2a=3b$.

**Answer: $3:2$**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-30.title: Compute a few iterates
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-30.body:
Direct calculation gives $f_2(x)=\frac{x-\sqrt3}{\sqrt3x+1}$ and $f_3(x)=-\frac1x$. Then $f_6(x)=f_3(f_3(x))=x$. Since $1986=6\cdot331$, $f_{1986}(x)=x$, so $f_{1986}(1985)=1985$.

**Answer: 1985**

nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-30.title: Rotation
nyciml-1985-86-fall-seniora-30.body:
Divide numerator and denominator by $2$: $f_1(x)=\frac{x\cos30^\circ-\sin30^\circ}{x\sin30^\circ+\cos30^\circ}$. If $x=\cot\theta$, then $f_1(x)=\cot(\theta+30^\circ)$. So $f_n(\cot\theta)=\cot(\theta+30n^\circ)$, and $30\cdot1986^\circ=59580^\circ=331\cdot180^\circ$, a multiple of $180^\circ$. Hence $f_{1986}$ is the identity.

**Answer: 1985**
